public_rationale: The field experiment reported two fewer hours on email per week among tool users in its second half, but no detected change in task quantity or composition [e5]. On July 17, 2026, Federal Reserve researchers described rising adoption and concentrated labor-market effects that had not broadened in the aggregate [e6]. On September 8, 2026, OpenAI reported more than one billion weekly active users and 2.5 million businesses using its products [e7]. These findings demonstrate some practical usefulness and reported reach, but neither establish an independently corroborated, broadly transformative turning point nor foreclose a future one [e5, e6, e7].
limitations: The field experiment measures specific workplace effects, not broad practical transformation.
The Federal Reserve assessment describes indicators available in July 2026, not all subsequent effects.
OpenAI's adoption figures are company-reported and do not measure realized benefits.
The forecast supplies neither a deadline nor a clear transformation threshold; finite nonoccurrence cannot establish its unlimited denial.
